html:
The Temple of the Emerald Buddha, inside the Grand Palace in Bangkok, Thailand, built from 1782 to 1784. It is the most sacred Buddhist temple in the country.

King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, began it when he moved the capital across the river to Bangkok in 1782, at the start of the Rattanakosin Kingdom. It has no monks living in it; it is the royal chapel. Its main hall houses the Emerald Buddha, a small figure carved from green stone. Legend says it was found in Chiang Rai in 1434; it later sat in Luang Prabang and Vientiane until the future Rama I took it from Vientiane in 1779. It is seen as the guardian of the kingdom, and the king himself changes its robes with the seasons.

The galleries around the temple are painted with the whole Ramakien, the Thai version of the Ramayana. The gilded spires, mosaics and guardian giants make it a showpiece of early Bangkok art, built to restore what was lost when Ayutthaya fell. See Siam, then Thailand.
sum: The Temple of the Emerald Buddha, inside the Grand Palace in Bangkok, Thailand, built from 1782 to 1784. It is the most sacred Buddhist temple in the country.
